CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Enrekang Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Enrekang Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Enrekang. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Regional Government. 5. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others directed towards women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 8. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 9. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, persons with disabilities, victims of maltreatment and/or neglect. 10. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 11. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Article 11
The family, in efforts to protect women's rights, has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social affairs, economics, politics, and culture; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 38
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be submitted by a complainant, which may be the victim, the family, the community, and/or community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
(2) The complainant as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit a complaint:
 a. directly;
 b. by telephone/short message service; or
 c. by letter/electronic mail.

Article 41
(1) Health services as referred to in Article 36 letter b include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty four) hours, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Special health services for children victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
(5) Comprehensive efforts to provide health services as referred to in paragraph (4), intended for victims of violence, abduction, neglect, economic and sexual exploitation, and trafficking in women and children, are guaranteed by the Regional Government.
(6) Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity.

Article 61
(1) Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 58
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence for the following year.

Article 45
(1) Women and children victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
   a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
   b. leaving the final decision to the victim/self-determination.
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants of the Advisory, Development and Preservation of Marriage Agency (BP4), Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), Ustad/Ulama, Priests, Pastors, Ministers, and other religious leaders who are gender responsive.

Part Three Parents/Guardians and/or Family
Article 14
Parents/guardians, and/or family shall undertake prevention against violations of the rights of women and children by means of:
a. protecting women and children from various acts of violation of the rights of women and children within the household.
b. supervising women and children in their activities inside or outside the home; and
c. providing opportunities for women and children to engage in dialogue and express their opinions democratically.

Paragraph 4
Social

CHAPTER XIV ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 62
(1) Every person or Institution that carries out the task of providing complaint handling services for victims of violence against women and children who violates the service principles as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. temporary revocation of license; or
d. revocation of license.
(3) Temporary revocation of license as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out after written warnings for 3 (three) consecutive times with a grace period of 7 (seven) working days.
(4) Revocation of license as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d, shall be carried out after temporary revocation with a grace period of 1 (one) month.

Article 47
(1) Repatriation as referred to in Article 36 letter e is intended to return women and children victims of violence to their region of origin.
(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) Regional Governments carry out repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 42
(1) Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence are intended to restore and develop the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social Rehabilitation Services as referred to in paragraph (1) include counseling services and spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that has duties and functions in the social field; and
b. service handling institutions.

Article 44
(1) Regional Governments are responsible for facilitating the availability of safe houses for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Safe houses aim to protect women and children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) Criteria for women and children victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Article 45
(1) Women and children victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
   a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
   b. leaving the final decision to the victim/self-determination.
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.
(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants of the Advisory, Development and Preservation of Marriage Agency (BP4), Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), Ustad/Ulama, Priests, Pastors, Ministers, and other religious leaders who are gender responsive.

Article 41
(1) Health services as referred to in Article 36 letter b include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty four) hours, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Special health services for children victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
(5) Comprehensive efforts to provide health services as referred to in paragraph (4), intended for victims of violence, abduction, neglect, economic and sexual exploitation, and trafficking in women and children, are guaranteed by the Regional Government.
(6) Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity.

Article 28
The Government is obligated to protect children in the school environment from acts of violence committed by teachers, school administrators or schoolmates.

Article 42
(1) Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence are intended to restore and develop the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that has duties and functions in the social field; and
b. service handling institutions.

(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be submitted by a complainant, which may be the victim, the family, the community, and/or community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.

Article 11
The family, in efforts to protect women's rights, has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social affairs, economics, politics, and culture; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations of women's rights in the household.

CHAPTER XIV ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 62
(1) Every person or Institution that carries out the task of providing complaint handling services for victims of violence against women and children who violates the service principles as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. temporary revocation of license; or
d. revocation of license.
(3) Temporary revocation of license as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out after written warnings for 3 (three) consecutive times with a grace period of 7 (seven) working days.
(4) Revocation of license as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d, shall be carried out after temporary revocation with a grace period of 1 (one) month.

Article 62

Article 9

(2) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 41
(1) Health services as referred to in Article 36 letter b include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty four) hours, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Special health services for children victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and

Article 14
Parents/guardians, and/or family shall undertake prevention against violations of the rights of women and children by means of:
a. protecting women and children from various acts of violation of the rights of women and children within the household.
b. supervising women and children in their activities inside or outside the home; and
c. providing opportunities for women and children to engage in dialogue and express their opinions democratically.

Article 44
(1) Regional Governments are responsible for facilitating the availability of safe houses for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Safe houses aim to protect women and children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) Criteria for women and children victims of violence who require safe houses include:

Article 62
(1) Every person or Institution that carries out the task of providing complaint handling services for victims of violence against women and children who violates the service principles as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. temporary revocation of license; or

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Enrekang Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Enrekang Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Enrekang. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Regional Government. 5. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others directed towards women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 8. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 9. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, persons with disabilities, victims of maltreatment and/or neglect. 10. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 11. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

CHAPTER XIV ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 62
(1) Every person or Institution that carries out the task of providing complaint handling services for victims of violence against women and children who violates the service principles as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Article 11
The family, in efforts to protect women's rights, has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social affairs, economics, politics, and culture; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations of women's rights in the household.

Part Three Parents/Guardians and/or Family
Article 14
Parents/guardians, and/or family shall undertake prevention against violations of the rights of women and children by means of:
a. protecting women and children from various acts of violation of the rights of women and children within the household.
b. supervising women and children in their activities inside or outside the home; and
c. providing opportunities for women and children to engage in dialogue and express their opinions democratically.

Article 9
Obligations and responsibilities of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.

Paragraph 3 Empowerment
(1) The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for women.
(2) The implementation of women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by the participation of the community and the business sector.

Article 35
The implementation of protection for women and children shall be carried out by cross-sectoral Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of women and children.

Paragraph 4
Social

Article 8
(1) In carrying out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1), the Regional Government establishes programs and activities for the protection of women and children, with a Regional Action Plan as the basis for the Regional Apparatus (PD) in implementing the protection of women and children in accordance with their duties and functions.
(2) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 15
(1) Regional Governments provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.
(2) The provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence for the following year.

Health

Article 41
(1) Health services as referred to in Article 36 letter b include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty four) hours, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Special health services for children victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and

Article 20
(1) A woman during the marriage bond has the same rights and responsibilities as her husband over all matters concerning their marital life, relationship with their children and ownership rights as well as management of joint property.
(2) After a court decision regarding divorce, a woman has the same rights and responsibilities as her former husband over all matters concerning their children, taking into account the best interests of the child.
(3) After a court decision regarding divorce, a woman has the same rights as her former husband over all matters concerning joint property without diminishing the rights of the child, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 61
(1) Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 45
(1) Women and children victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
   a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
   b. leaving the final decision to the victim/self-determination.
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Enrekang Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Enrekang Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Enrekang. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Regional Government. 5. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others directed towards women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 8. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 9. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, persons with disabilities, victims of maltreatment and/or neglect. 10. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 11. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

1. Region is Enrekang Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Enrekang Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Enrekang. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Regional Government. 5. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others directed towards women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 8. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 9. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, persons with disabilities, victims of maltreatment and/or neglect. 10. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 11. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Article 9
Obligations and responsibilities of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.

Article 61
(1) Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others directed towards women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 8. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, persons with disabilities, victims of maltreatment and/or neglect. 10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Health

Article 35
The implementation of protection for women and children shall be carried out by cross-sectoral Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of women and children.

Article 8
(1) In carrying out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1), the Regional Government establishes programs and activities for the protection of women and children, with a Regional Action Plan as the basis for the Regional Apparatus (PD) in implementing the protection of women and children in accordance with their duties and functions.
(2) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 41
(1) Health services as referred to in Article 36 letter b include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty four) hours, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Special health services for children victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

Article 57
The PD responsible for planning affairs coordinates programs for the protection of women and children from violence, exploitation and discrimination with related PDs.

a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social affairs, economics, politics, and culture; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 61
(1) Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.

Article 44
(1) Regional Governments are responsible for facilitating the availability of safe houses for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Safe houses aim to protect women and children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) Criteria for women and children victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 48
(1) The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children is carried out by the Regional Government.

b. LK3; and
c. Satgas PPA.

Part Three Parents/Guardians and/or Family
Article 14
Parents/guardians, and/or family shall undertake prevention against violations of the rights of women and children by means of:
a. protecting women and children from various acts of violation of the rights of women and children within the household.
b. supervising women and children in their activities inside or outside the home; and
c. providing opportunities for women and children to engage in dialogue and express their opinions democratically.

Article 19
Protection of Women's Micro Economy includes:
a. obtaining opportunities to conduct business activities in the household environment; and
b. obtaining economic empowerment facilities especially for women heads of households.

Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Enrekang Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Enrekang Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Enrekang. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Regional Government. 5. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others directed towards women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 8. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 9. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, persons with disabilities, victims of maltreatment and/or neglect. 10. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 11. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Enrekang Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Enrekang Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Enrekang. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Regional Government. 5. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others directed towards women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 8. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 9. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, persons with disabilities, victims of maltreatment and/or neglect. 10. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 11. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Article 15
(1) Regional Governments provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for women in order to obtain optimal health status.
(2) The provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

Article 42
(1) Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence are intended to restore and develop the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social Rehabilitation Services as referred to in paragraph (1) include counseling services and spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that has duties and functions in the social field; and
b. service handling institutions.

CHAPTER XVI CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 65
This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.
In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Enrekang Regency.
